newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerians vote in numbers, no violence reported.
newsitem.headline: Algerians vote in numbers, no violence reported.

text.p: Algerians were turning out in large numbers on Thursday to vote in a controversial referendum on changing the constitution and there were no reports of violence as threatened by Islamic militants, official media said.
Three hours after polls opened nearly 23 percent of more than 16 million eligible voters had cast their ballots, Algerian state-run radio said, quoting the interior ministry.
Official media said voting was taking place peacefully and there were no reports of violence.

Moslem guerrillas, waging a five-year guerrilla war against the North African country's secular government, have vowed to disrupt the poll and warned that rebels would "strike the neck" of any one who dared leave their home to vote.

Opposition parties have either called for a boycott or urged voters to say "no" to the proposed changes in the referendum which would strengthen the position of President Liamine Zeroual and bar Islamic fundamentalists from using religion as a platform to gain power.
